# 1 Kings Chapter 19 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** And-Ahab told Jezebel ʾet-all that Elijah had-done, and-ʾet all how he-killed ʾet-all the-prophets with-the-sword.

**2** And-Jezebel sent a-messenger to-Elijah, saying, "Thus may-the-gods do to-me and-thus may-they-add, if by-this time tomorrow I-do-not make your-life as-the-life-of one-of-them."

**3** And-he-saw, and-he-arose, and-went for-his-life, and-came to-Beer-sheba, that belongs-to-Judah, and-left his-servant there.

**4** And-he went into-the-wilderness a-day's journey, and-came and-sat under a-broom-bush, and-asked ʾet-his-soul to-die, and-said, "Enough! Now, YHWH, take my-life, for I-am-not better than-my-fathers."

**5** And-he-lay-down and-slept under a-broom-bush. And-behold — an-angel touching-him, and-said to-him, "Arise, eat."

**6** And-he-looked, and-behold — at his-head a-cake-of coals and-a-jar-of water. And-he-ate and-drank and-lay-down again.

**7** And-the-angel-of YHWH returned a-second-time and-touched-him and-said, "Arise, eat, for the-journey is-too-great for-you."

**8** And-he-arose and-ate and-drank, and-went in-the-strength-of that food forty days and-forty nights to-Horeb, the-mountain-of God.

**9** And-he-came there to the-cave and-lodged there. And-behold — the-word-of YHWH came to-him, and-said to-him, "What are-you-doing here, Elijah?"

**10** And-he-said, "I-have-been-very-zealous for-YHWH, the-God-of Hosts, for the-sons-of Israel have-forsaken your-covenant, ʾet-your-altars they-have-torn-down, and-ʾet-your-prophets they-have-killed with-the-sword. And-I-am-left, I alone, and-they-seek my-life to-take-it."

**11** And-he-said, "Go-out and-stand on the-mountain before YHWH." And-behold — YHWH passing-by. And-a-great and-strong wind tearing mountains and-shattering rocks before YHWH — YHWH was-not in-the-wind. And-after the-wind — an-earthquake — YHWH was-not in-the-earthquake.

**12** And-after the-earthquake — a-fire — YHWH was-not in-the-fire. And-after the-fire — a-sound-of thin silence.

**13** And-it-was when-Elijah heard, and-he-wrapped his-face in-his-mantle and-went-out and-stood at-the-entrance-of the-cave. And-behold — a-voice came-to-him, and-said, "What are-you-doing here, Elijah?"

**14** And-he-said, "I-have-been-very-zealous for-YHWH, the-God-of Hosts, for the-sons-of Israel have-forsaken your-covenant, ʾet-your-altars they-have-torn-down, and-ʾet-your-prophets they-have-killed with-the-sword. And-I-am-left, I alone, and-they-seek my-life to-take-it."

**15** And-YHWH said to-him, "Go, return on-your-way to the-wilderness-of Damascus. And-when-you-come, you-shall-anoint Hazael as-king over Aram.

**16** And-ʾet-Jehu son-of Nimshi you-shall-anoint as-king over Israel. And-ʾet-Elisha son-of Shaphat, from-Abel-meholah, you-shall-anoint as-prophet in-your-place.

**17** And-it-shall-be — the-one-who-escapes from-the-sword-of Hazael, Jehu will-kill. And-the-one-who-escapes from-the-sword-of Jehu, Elisha will-kill.

**18** And-I-will-leave in-Israel seven thousand — all the-knees that have-not bowed to-the-Baal, and-every mouth that has-not kissed-him."

**19** And-he-went from-there and-found Elisha son-of Shaphat, and-he was-plowing — twelve yoke before-him, and-he was with-the-twelfth. And-Elijah passed-by to-him and-threw his-mantle upon-him.

**20** And-he-left ʾet-the-oxen and-ran after Elijah and-said, "Let-me-kiss, please, my-father and-my-mother, and-I-will-follow after-you." And-he-said to-him, "Go, return, for what have-I-done to-you?"

**21** And-he-returned from-after-him, and-took ʾet-the-yoke-of the-oxen and-slaughtered-them, and-with-the-equipment-of the-oxen he-boiled their-flesh, and-gave to-the-people and-they-ate. And-he-arose and-went after Elijah and-served-him.

---
## EMET Textual Notes

1. **19:4 — "I-am-not better than-my-fathers"**: The prophet who just defeated 450 prophets of Baal now collapses under one woman's threat. Elijah's depression is as real as his victory — the text refuses to idealize prophetic life.
2. **19:8 — "forty days and-forty nights"**: The same duration as Moses on Sinai (Exod 24:18) and Israel in the wilderness. Elijah's journey to Horeb deliberately recapitulates the Mosaic experience.
3. **19:12 — "a-sound-of thin silence" (קוֹל דְּמָמָה דַקָּה)**: The most debated phrase in the chapter. Not wind, earthquake, or fire — but qol demamah daqqah: a voice of thin/fine silence. God's presence comes in the absence of spectacle.
4. **19:18 — "seven thousand"**: God's hidden remnant. Elijah thought he was alone; God has seven thousand faithful. The prophet's despair was based on incomplete information.
5. **19:21 — burning the equipment**: Elisha destroys his farming tools — an irreversible act. He cannot return to plowing. The call to prophecy demands total commitment.

— EMET
